posts.title: 2026.33: The CapEx Train Keeps Rolling
posts.summary: The best Stratechery content from the week of August 10, 2026, including the capital constraint, AI writing, and a tale of two cities.
bullets: The AI industry is shifting toward creative financial engineering, such as Nvidia's new funding mechanisms, to bridge the gap between massive capital expenditure and currently unproven AI revenue models.

Google and other major players are increasingly utilizing equity markets to sustain AI infrastructure investment, effectively expanding the potential financial blast radius if AI returns fail to materialize.

New EU regulations mandating the labeling of AI-generated content are being met with industry resistance, as critics argue such mandates ignore the historical evolution of idea propagation and the shifting societal norms regarding machine-assisted output.

The divergence between New York City's resilient financial sector and Hollywood's declining local production base highlights how network effects can protect some industries from political pressure while leaving others vulnerable to geographic outsourcing.

posts.title: Li Auto's chip ambitions extend from assisted driving to data centers, report says
posts.summary:
Li Auto is exploring an in-house cloud inference chip, and the project is still at an early stage.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto is in the early stages of developing an in-house cloud inference chip to handle workloads currently managed by GPUs.
The project aims to leverage the dataflow architecture used in the company's vehicle-side assisted driving chips to reduce R&D costs through shared design and software tools.
While technically feasible, the company faces significant challenges in achieving cost-competitive inference performance compared to established GPU-based data center solutions.
The cloud-side chip must address complex requirements such as dynamic batching, cluster scheduling, and high-bandwidth memory, which differ significantly from vehicle-side constraints.

posts.title: Li Auto's L6 tops 400,000 cumulative deliveries as revamped model revives demand
posts.summary:
The Li L6 delivered about 9,000 units in the first half of August, compared with just 2,716 for the whole of July, based on CnEVPost-compiled data.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto's L6 SUV has surpassed 400,000 cumulative deliveries in less than 27 months, cementing its status as a core volume driver for the company.
The model experienced a sharp demand rebound in August, with approximately 9,000 units delivered in the first half of the month following the July 16 launch of a revamped version.
The new L6 features significant technical upgrades, including a larger 51 kWh battery for 300 km of electric range and the integration of the in-house Mach M100 assisted driving chip.
The successful refresh of the L6 is a critical component of Li Auto's broader strategy to overhaul its L-series lineup and recover from a mid-year sales slump.

posts.title: Geely Farizon's first overseas plant starts operations in Indonesia
posts.summary:
The first locally assembled V8E all-electric logistics vehicle rolled off the line on August 13 at a plant about 80 kilometers southeast of Jakarta.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely Farizon has commenced operations at its first overseas knock-down (KD) plant in Indonesia, located southeast of Jakarta.
The facility began production with the V8E all-electric logistics vehicle, which has been specifically calibrated for local road conditions and tropical climates.
The move to local assembly is a strategic effort to bypass import tariffs, streamline supply chains, and meet tightening localization requirements in the Southeast Asian market.
Geely Farizon plans to gradually expand its localized product lineup and integrate further into the Indonesian industrial chain to support long-term growth.

posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
Lam Research and ASE expansions; data center shifts; CPO system architecture initiative; 2D-transistor interface solution; USENIX HW security; patent suits; image sensors; programmable AI memtransistor; Nvidia's new plan; earnings; Tier IV's L4 auto chip.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: ASE subsidiary SPIL is investing $3.1 billion in a new Taiwan-based facility to expand CoWoS capacity for AI chips, with production slated to begin in 2028.

Data center architecture is shifting toward 1-megawatt racks, necessitating fundamental changes in cooling, power delivery, and the integration of optical interconnects to manage AI-driven compute demands.
Rhodium Group projects that China's legacy-chip capacity will reach nearly 50% of global output by 2030, even as the nation faces ongoing restrictions on leading-edge AI semiconductor technology.

Lam Research has committed $3 billion over five years to expand its R&D lab network by 50%, while simultaneously partnering with NY Creates to train 3,500 students in semiconductor process integration.
Industry experts are increasingly advocating for smaller, open-source AI models that reduce the reliance on massive data centers by enabling efficient performance on local hardware.

posts.title: Building a practical path to post-quantum cryptography
posts.summary: Quantum computing has alternated between breakthrough darling and overhyped promise in technology circles. Its powerful new capabilities come with a threat to break current cryptography, but for business leaders navigating the noise, the signal should be clear: post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is a manageable evolution, not a crisis. The mathematics behind today’s encrypted digital transactions may…
bullets: Experts estimate a 50-50 probability that quantum computers will be capable of breaking 2048-bit RSA encryption by 2040, necessitating a long-term strategic shift in cybersecurity.
Enterprises are advised to prioritize protection against 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks, where sensitive data is intercepted today for future decryption by quantum-capable adversaries.
The transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is framed as a manageable, phased evolution rather than an immediate crisis, allowing firms to modernize infrastructure without systemic disruption.

posts.title: Flock is tightening its rules in response to a growing surveillance backlash
posts.summary: The police-tech giant Flock is announcing today that it will change officers’ access to its nationwide network of license plate readers, in an apparent effort to quell a growing backlash and win back contracts lost amid concerns about mass surveillance and police abuse. Several changes aim directly at a problem that has made recent headlines:…
bullets: Flock is implementing mandatory criminal case number requirements and automated auditing for its 120,000-camera network to mitigate widespread reports of officer abuse and stalking.
Despite these new guardrails, critics and civil liberties groups remain skeptical, noting that officers have historically bypassed similar safeguards by entering generic or mocking data.

The company is facing significant reputational and financial risk as cities terminate contracts due to concerns over mass surveillance and the lack of independent verification for its internal auditing tools.

posts.title: The 1-Megawatt Rack Debate
posts.summary:
Is it better to cram more compute into each rack or rethink the architecture?
The post The 1-Megawatt Rack Debate appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Is it better to cram more compute into each rack or rethink the architecture?

Key Takeaways:
Data centers are gearing up for a future in which a single rack could consume as much power as an entire building.

Hyperscalers already are collaborating to establish standards for 1-megawatt racks, and as AI workloads grow more continuous, autonomous, and power-intensive, there is an ongoing debate about whether developing...
Technologies like optics, specialized silicon, and high-voltage DC systems can enable a more fragmented future with distributed workloads and reduced density.
At least for now, data center operators and cloud service providers (CSPs) are preparing for the move to 1-megawatt racks, which will require foundational changes to the data center architecture.

posts.title: Copper’s Grip On AI Scaling Is Starting To Slip
posts.summary:
As AI clusters push beyond rack-scale limits, optical interconnects and circuit switching are reshaping how data centers scale. 
The post Copper’s Grip On AI Scaling Is Starting To Slip appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: As AI clusters push beyond rack-scale limits, optical interconnects and circuit switching are reshaping how data centers scale.

Key Takeaways:
Data-center network fabrics are undergoing another architectural shift as optical interconnects assume a larger role in AI-cluster connectivity, extending into scale-up domains and influencing overall...
Scale-up has typically been defined as a single rack with copper interconnect, with programmers using memory semantics.
That definition is getting fuzzier.
“The old rule that scale-up is copper and scale-out is optical is starting to blur,” said Steven Woo, fellow and distinguished inventor at Rambus.

posts.title: BYD's flash charging Qin Max sedan goes on sale in China for under $15,000
posts.summary:
The BYD Qin Max is the flagship of the Qin family, available in EV and DM-i versions.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD has launched the Qin Max sedan, priced between 99,900 and 143,900 yuan, as a strategic effort to revitalize its flagship Qin lineup following a significant sales decline this year.
The EV variant features BYD's second-generation Blade Battery and ultra-fast 'flash charging' technology, capable of charging from 10% to 97% in just nine minutes.
The DM-i plug-in hybrid model achieves a combined range of 2,370 km and a fuel consumption rate of 2.59 liters per 100 km, setting a new efficiency benchmark for its class.
The vehicle integrates advanced technology, including LiDAR-based 'God's Eye B' navigation assist and an AI agent named Didi Xia, targeting younger consumer demographics.

posts.title: 2D GAA CFETs Need Contact And Parasitic Co-Optimization At A2 Node (imec)
posts.summary:
Researchers from imec published a technical paper titled “Are Gate-All-Around 2D CFETs the Optimal Architecture for the A2 Node and Beyond?” Abstract Excerpt: “Here, we develop an A2-oriented 2D CFET integration flow with a CPP of 36 nm and Lg of 10 nm and present initial demonstrations of several key process modules. Despite their atomically... » read more
The post 2D GAA CFETs Need Contact And Parasitic Co-Optimization At A2 Node (imec) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Imec research indicates that 2D Gate-All-Around (GAA) CFETs do not offer a contacted poly pitch (CPP) scaling advantage over traditional Silicon GAA CFETs at the A2 node.
The study highlights that contact formation constraints impose a minimum CPP of 36nm, necessitating rigorous co-optimization of contacts and parasitics.
The team utilized a multiscale power-performance-area (PPA) evaluation framework, incorporating quantum transport simulations and circuit-level benchmarking to assess the viability of 2D materials.

These findings suggest that while 2D materials are promising, their integration into A2-node architectures requires significant process module innovation to overcome current physical scaling limitations.

posts.title: Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure
posts.summary:
112G PHY IP for linear optics to reduce power, latency and thermal load for high-speed data movement in AI and data center systems.
The post Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Synopsys has introduced the industry's first 112G PHY IP compliant with the OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 standard, enabling DSP-less host-to-module connectivity.
Transitioning to linear optics can reduce module power consumption by up to 50%, significantly lowering thermal loads in high-density AI data center racks.
The solution eliminates the need for power-hungry DSPs and retimers, providing a scalable path toward 224G/448G interconnects and Co-Packaged Optics (CPO).
By meeting or exceeding CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 specifications for jitter and eye-closure, this IP provides a standardized, interoperable foundation for next-generation AI infrastructure.

posts.title: Self-Supervised Layout Generation To Fix Advanced-Node DRVs (Nvidia, Duke)
posts.summary:
Researchers from NVIDIA and Duke University published a technical paper titled “SCALE: Self-Supervised Constraint-Aware Layout GEneration for Local P&R DRV Fixing at Advanced Nodes.” Abstract “As semiconductor manufacturing advances toward sub-2nm nodes, local place-and-route (P&R) design-rule violation (DRV) fixing is increasingly limited by complex rule interactions, dense multi-layer routing geometries, and foundry-specific constraints. While Large... » read more
The post Self-Supervised Layout Generation To Fix Advanced-Node DRVs (Nvidia, Duke) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers from NVIDIA and Duke University developed SCALE, a self-supervised framework designed to automate the fixing of design-rule violations (DRVs) at sub-2nm nodes.
The framework utilizes a domain-adapted Vision-Language Model (VLM) that learns to reconstruct masked layout polygons, providing geometric guidance for complex routing issues.
SCALE improves the solve rates of existing automated agents by 12% to 25%, achieving up to 97% success on real-world sub-2nm layout cases.
By automating the repair of spacing, width, and color-spacing violations, this technology addresses the growing bottleneck of manual layout fixing in advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

posts.title: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
posts.summary: Business and technology leaders need no convincing that the time of agentic AI is here. Organizations are rapidly adopting agents, and few executives doubt the technology’s potential to transform work. But many organizations find that realizing the desired return on investment (ROI) from AI hinges on having the right foundation, with inadequate infrastructure and data…
bullets: A survey of 300 executives reveals that legacy data infrastructure is the primary bottleneck preventing the effective scaling of autonomous AI agents.
Current enterprise AI agents have access to an average of only 45% of company data, while top-performing 'data leaders' ensure access to over 70%.
Gartner predicts that AI agents will automate or augment 50% of business decisions by 2027, making the modernization of data access systems a critical priority for ROI.
Successful deployment of agentic AI requires moving beyond simple question-answering systems to providing agents with real-time, frictionless access to structured and unstructured operational data.

posts.title: Xiaomi EV delivers 31,267 units in July, 39% of annual target
posts.summary:
Xiaomi EV needs average monthly deliveries of nearly 67,000 units over the remaining 5 months to achieve its full-year target of 550,000 units.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi EV delivered 31,267 vehicles in July, marking a fourth consecutive month above the 30,000-unit threshold but representing a 9.99% decline from June.

With only 216,322 units delivered in the first seven months, Xiaomi has achieved just 39% of its 550,000-unit annual target, necessitating a significant production ramp-up to nearly 67,000 units per month for the remainder of the year.
The company is pivoting toward the extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) market with its new Sky Nomad series, positioning the N90 Max and N70 Max to compete directly with Li Auto and Aito.
Market reception to the new product line remains uncertain, as evidenced by a 7.28% drop in Xiaomi's Hong Kong-listed shares following the initial pricing announcement on July 31.
